I have no sequence-database or variant-lookup tool in this session (no NCBI/Ensembl/ClinVar access, no network), so this answer comes from my own knowledge rather than a live lookup. I've flagged the one or two items where I'd want you to verify against the primary source.

## Identity

**rs113993960 = CFTR F508del** — far and away the best-known cystic fibrosis variant.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Gene | *CFTR* (CF transmembrane conductance regulator), 7q31.2 |
| Location | Exon 11 (exon 10 in the older numbering) |
| HGVS coding | NM_000492.4:c.1521_1523delCTT |
| HGVS protein | p.Phe508del |
| Legacy names | ΔF508, F508del, delta-F508, c.1521_1523delCTT |
| Type | In-frame 3-bp deletion → loss of one phenylalanine residue |
| GRCh38 | chr7:~117,559,590–117,559,592 *(verify exact left-align in dbSNP/ClinVar — deletion normalization shifts the reported start)* |
| ClinVar | Pathogenic; Variation ID 7105 *(ID from memory — confirm)* |

## Clinical significance

**Pathogenic for cystic fibrosis**, autosomal recessive, with expert-panel-level review status in ClinVar (CFTR2 / ClinGen CFTR Variant Curation Expert Panel). It is a **Class II (folding/trafficking) defect**: the protein misfolds, is degraded by ER quality control, and little to no CFTR reaches the apical membrane.

Key points for interpreting the report:

- **Zygosity is everything.** A single F508del allele makes someone an unaffected **carrier**. Disease requires two pathogenic CFTR alleles — F508del/F508del, or F508del in *trans* with another pathogenic variant (compound heterozygote). If the report only lists the rs ID without zygosity and without a second allele, the genotype is not yet interpretable. Ask for zygosity and for the full CFTR variant list (including whether the panel covered the common non-F508del alleles and the poly-TG/poly-T tract).
- **Phenotype when biallelic:** classic CF — pancreatic insufficiency in the large majority, progressive obstructive lung disease, elevated sweat chloride, CF-related diabetes, male infertility from congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens. F508del is a "severe"/minimal-function allele; residual-function variants in *trans* soften the phenotype.
- **Epidemiology:** accounts for roughly 70% of CF alleles worldwide and ~2/3 to 70% in European-ancestry populations; carrier frequency on the order of 1 in 25 in Northern Europeans. gnomAD non-Finnish European allele frequency is on the order of 0.7%.
- **Therapeutic relevance — this is the actionable part.** F508del is the gating variant for CFTR modulator eligibility. Elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (Trikafta/Kaftrio) is indicated for patients with **at least one** F508del allele; lumacaftor/ivacaftor (Orkambi) and tezacaftor/ivacaftor (Symdeko/Symkevi) require two copies or one copy plus a responsive variant. A positive F508del finding in an affected patient should prompt a modulator-eligibility discussion.
- **Other considerations:** carrier testing/genetic counselling for the patient's partner and relatives; F508del is on the ACMG recommended carrier-screening panel.

To confirm any of the above against primary sources, the canonical references are dbSNP rs113993960, ClinVar, and **CFTR2.org**, which gives the curated clinical consequence and modulator-response classification for each CFTR allele.

## ANSWER

**Gene:** *CFTR* (7q31.2), exon 11.
**Variant:** F508del / p.Phe508del / c.1521_1523delCTT — the ΔF508 3-bp in-frame deletion.
**Clinical significance:** **Pathogenic** for cystic fibrosis (autosomal recessive); most common CF-causing allele (~70% of CF alleles). One copy = carrier; two pathogenic alleles = classic CF. Class II folding/trafficking defect. Confers eligibility for CFTR modulator therapy (elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor with ≥1 copy).
*Source: my own knowledge — no database lookup tool was available in this session; verify in ClinVar/dbSNP/CFTR2.*
